en.title: Optimal Split Paying the Maximum of Each Segment
en.description:
Cut the entire integer array, keeping its original order, into non-empty contiguous segments, each of length ≤threshold; the cost of a segment is its maximum value. Find the minimum total cost over all segments. Negative integers are allowed, and segment lengths are not forced to equal the limit.

The input/output protocol and the explicitly marked supplementary constraints were compiled by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first line contains n threshold, and the second line contains the array. The original text gives no numeric bounds; this site adds 1≤threshold≤n≤5000 and −10⁹≤element≤10⁹.
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 10; -6; 20. The examples were rechecked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: Let dp[i] be the minimum cost of the first i items. Enumerate the start of the last segment backward while maintaining its maximum, and update dp[i].
